body.text: Junk journals are built from paper that has already lived a bit (envelopes, tickets, tags, a torn map), and a handful of well-chosen buys make the pages sturdier, prettier and more fun to make.

This guide is what to buy: the four things that make the biggest difference, the longer list for when you're hooked and what can wait. For how to begin, with your first page step by step, see the how-to linked at the end.
The four things that make the biggest difference
Each one is described by what it does, so you can choose the ones you like in any shop.

items: **A journal with thick pages.** This is the one place a little quality matters. Glue and layers make thin pages buckle, so look for heavier paper, a binding that opens flat and a size you'll carry around. A sketchbook, a plain notebook or a thrifted hardback all work; with a used book, glue a few pages together to thicken them and tear others out to make room.

**A mixed set of washi tape.** Tape is how scrappy paper starts to look like it belongs together. Look for a few plain colors alongside the patterns, so there's something quiet to balance the busy rolls. It's usually sold as removable, but test a scrap on your paper first.
**A fine pen.** One black fine pen handles captions and borders, and an accent color covers doodles. Test that the ink doesn't smear over dry glue before committing a whole page to it.
**One sticker set in a single style.** Pick a lane, whether botanical, vintage labels or small icons. One set you reuse beats five you scatter.

body.text: **What makes it easier:** a glue stick or tape runner kept next to the journal, so layers go down fast and you can keep going on the same page.

optional: A mixed set of washi tape
A small stamp and ink pad
A bone folder, or the back of a spoon, for smoothing

body.title: Your first junk journal basket
body.dek: A thick-paged journal, a washi tape set, a glue stick or tape runner, a fine pen and some vintage-style paper cover pages that are sturdier and prettier from page one. Already own one? Start with whichever you're missing.

body.text: Fun extras for after page three

items: **Large vintage-paper bundles.** Wait to see whether you lean soft and aged or bold and bright.
**Punches and die-cut machines.** You can tear and cut by hand for a long time.
**Wax seals, charms and embellishments.** Add one when a page asks for it.
**Stronger adhesives.** Reach for one only if chunky items keep falling off.
**The first basket:** a purpose-made journal with thick pages, a washi tape set, a glue stick or tape runner and a fine pen.
**The second basket:** one sticker set in a single style, a small stamp and ink pad, and a few extra pens and papers.
**Already on the shelf:** a notebook you own, a half-used glue stick and scraps will start page one while the basket is on its way.

body.text: Compare listings before you choose, since sizes, paper weights and pack counts differ. For more starter ideas, see [affordable hobbies](/journal/affordable-hobbies-under-25).

items: **Pick a palette first.** Three colors, say cream, deep green and a warm red, keep every purchase compatible.
**Buy for this weekend's page,** not the one you might make in June.
**Check paper weight** when a listing mentions it. Heavier paper is often easier to layer.

**Read acid-free and archival labels with care.** They are marketing terms with no single official standard, and acid-free alone does not make something safe for photographs. For photos you care about, use copies rather than originals, and look for adhesives that say they passed the Photographic Activity Test (ISO 18916).

body.text: Kitchen-drawer scissors and a ruler, a half-used glue stick and one pen you like will carry you through the first few pages. Paper with a past is lovely material: envelope liners, receipts, tickets, tags, brown paper bags, magazine pages, cereal-box cardboard for sturdy backgrounds and pockets.

Keep an envelope in your bag for a week and drop in anything flat and interesting. Then make one page from only what you own, and note the one thing you truly wished you had. That is your first purchase: a better journal, a tape set or a tape runner will usually make the difference.

Weighing up bundles? See [Creative Hobby Starter Kits That Are Actually Worth Considering](/journal/creative-hobby-starter-kits-worth-considering). Ready to make the first page? Head to [How to Start Junk Journaling](/journal/how-to-start-junk-journaling).
